The management overlay (tools/red_team_management_models.py) confines runtime graph change to exactly four reviewed nodes (two enum vocabularies, two appended union tails), proven by tools/test_red_team_management_models.py:17-24, and fails closed on unreviewed vendor keywords, patterns, defaults, additionalProperties policies, divergent masked counterparts and renamed baseline models. The planned enum split is real in generated code: TargetConnectionType/ResponseMode keep only frozen variants with Unknown(String) (generated.rs:174153, :162443) while TargetCreateRequestConnectionType/TargetCreateRequestResponseMode name VERTEX_AI/N8N/REALTIME (:174692, :174763), asserted in crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_models.rs:119-164. Typed projections relocate four formerly raw keys into Patch fields with lossless raw fallback and typed-over-raw precedence (generated.rs:9313-9392), exercised by 84 vendor-derived cases across three modes (red_team_management_fixtures.rs:57-88). The five target response declarations are served by the retained shared root s012107 with an explicit per-operation supersetJustification and stated comparison limits (contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/compatibility-decisions.json:5526-5530, :6269-6273), and all five operations are wire-asserted for method, path, operation name, both response modes, masked and credential-bearing branches, and secret-free Debug/error output (red_team_management_contracts.rs:345-459). The profiling filter is validated against the vendor ProfilingStatusFilter vocabulary before token acquisition or dispatch and propagates unchanged through list/pages/items/list_all with exact query-pair counts (targets.rs:84-91; contracts test :466-558), while legacy `status` is transmitted untranslated with accurate rustdoc naming the five values upstream no longer declares (targets.rs:26-46). Evidence is executed, not merely registered: the attempt-01 checks file records ~68 checks at the reviewed source, every one exit_code 0 and source_unchanged true, including cargo fmt/check/clippy/test/doc on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 over minimal/default/all/red-team/gateway/json-unification sets (the management tests are feature-gated on red-team, and the red-team sets ran), generate_models.py --check and --verify-fixtures (27479 typed cases), management_fixtures.py --check, g25_report.py --check, full tools/test_*.py discovery, native-exports on both toolchains with 3820 frozen capabilities retained, and both clean packaged consumers followed by --verify-package-receipts. findings.required_fix: Add a new scope_revision for this chunk listing crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team_management.rs, crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json, contracts/red-team-management-union-extensions.json and crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_models.rs (preserving the attempt-1 revision unchanged), or state explicitly in the phase record that these artifacts are covered by the enclosing phase review.

findings.description: The plan (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:110-111) requires recording observable Unknown(JsonValue)-to-named-variant transitions. Both extended unions have an Unknown(JsonValue) fallback (generated.rs:172271, :172560), so payloads that previously decoded as Unknown now decode as Variant5(VertexAIConnectionParams) and Variant3(MultiTurnClientSessionConfig) — for example {"type":"client_session"}, which fails the Variant2 stateless literal. The overlay ledger records the appended branches but no artifact in this chunk states the transition as an observable consumer-visible change, and CHANGELOG.md contains no entry yet.
findings.required_fix: Record the transition in a source-bound artifact in this chunk — e.g. a short field alongside runtimeUnionExtensions in the overlay ledger and a sentence in the generated G25 management addendum — naming the two unions and the previously-Unknown shapes, so the phase 24 changelog can cite it rather than re-derive it.

findings.description: The union-case acceptance booleans (requestAccepted/responseAccepted for valid, missing-required, wrong-type and loose-format Vertex cases and the three multi-turn cases) are hand-authored in the deriving tool, unlike the G25 corpus whose expected outcomes come from an independent Zod/AJV oracle. Inputs and required/pattern sets are vendor-derived, so this is reasonable, but the evidenceBoundary string at line 96 describes the corpus only as "vendor-derived shape and independent preservation witnesses" and does not disclose that acceptance expectations are reviewed authored values.
findings.required_fix: Extend the evidenceBoundary text (or add an explicit expectationsOrigin field) to state that union acceptance expectations are reviewed, vendor-schema-derived authored values rather than independent validator-oracle outputs; optionally cross-check them against an independent oracle as done for G25.

findings.description: `import copy` is unused in this test module.

The reviewed doc comment for VertexAIConnectionRedactParams is injected after the derive and #[non_exhaustive] attributes (lines 241-246). It still renders in rustdoc, but it reads inconsistently with every other generated declaration, where docs precede attributes.
findings.required_fix: In tools/generate_models.py's replace_once anchor for this declaration, target the attribute block so the doc comment is emitted before #[derive]/#[non_exhaustive].

Enum split is real in generated code, not just claimed: generated.rs:174153-174165 (TargetConnectionType: 11 frozen variants + Unknown(String)) versus :174692-174707 (TargetCreateRequestConnectionType adds VERTEXAI, N8N), and :162443-162449 versus :174763-174769 (TargetCreateRequestResponseMode adds REALTIME). Asserted end-to-end in red_team_management_models.rs:135-164 and at graph level in :119-132 (s012061 rejects REALTIME in Request mode).

Union extension is positional and prefix-pinned: tools/red_team_management_models.py:212-215 appends exactly one branch after asserting the legacy branch count, :267-283 verifies the emitted tail against the reviewed ledger and strips it before the strict baseline comparison, and tools/test_red_team_management_models.py:145-165 proves prefix reorder, tail retype and missing tail all raise. generated.rs:172267-172271 and :172554-172560 show Variant3/Variant5 appended ahead of the Unknown(JsonValue) fallback.

Behaviour is asserted for all seven value kinds in red_team_management_fixtures.rs:57-88 (84 cases x 3 modes, with typedPresence and secret-free Debug), for collision/unset restore in red_team_management_contracts.rs:572-602, and for raw passthrough of wrong-typed values in :182-201.

Five response declarations: targets.rs:164-301 routes create/get/update/probe/update_profile through the retained shared root TargetResponseSchema; the superset decision is explicitly recorded per operation with justification and limits in contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/compatibility-decisions.json:5526-5530 (TargetRedactSchema) and :6269-6273 (TargetSchema). red_team_management_contracts.rs:345-459 exercises 5 providers x 4 auth shapes x 2 response modes across all five operations, asserting operation names, methods, paths, raw byte equality in ResponseWithoutDefaults, validator-normalized equality in Response, and absence of the synthetic secret in Debug.

limitations: Read-only review: I executed no commands, so all pass/fail evidence comes from the recorded attempt-01 checks file. The docs/checks/phase-23-*.json receipts referenced by the checks file are untracked in the working tree at review time, so their contents are outside the reviewed source hash; I relied on the checkpoint_bindings hashes recorded in the checks file.

Offline scope only. Nothing here establishes live service acceptance: the clean package runs build 0.2.2 bytes in worktrees under .local (not inspected), the corpus states its own evidence boundary, and tenant qualification, changelog and release-version selection belong to phase 24.

Cross-chunk artifacts (contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/compatibility-decisions.json, the frozen 0.2.2 old-consumer sources, CHANGELOG.md, .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml) were consulted only to validate this chunk's design claims; they are scoped to the package-security chunk and were not reviewed for their own acceptance.
